# Project overview
This script performs a clonal group analysis on Aspergillus isolates. It merges PLINK genomic distance data with metadata (origin, location, and variants) and uses network analysis to identify clusters of highly related strains (DST > 0.998).

## Set-up
First, we clear the environment, load the necessary tidyverse libraries, and import the genomic and metadata files.

```{r environmental, echo= F}
# Load genomic distance data (PLINK)
plink_df <- read.table(glue::glue("{data}/ATL.core.genome"), header = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(SNP_dif = IBS0 + IBS1)

# Load variant and metadata info
variant_info <- read.csv(glue::glue("{data}/2026_variant_info.csv")) %>%
  select(isolate, variant) %>% 
  rename(strain = isolate)

info_df <- read.csv(glue::glue("{data}/2026_meta_info.csv")) %>% 
  select(-1)

# Load California MIC data and clean species names
calif_df <- read.table(glue::glue("{data}/1.Wang_etal_MIC.txt"), header = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate_at(c('ITC', 'VOR', 'POS'), ~ gsub('>', '', .)) %>% 
  mutate_at(c('ITC', 'VOR', 'POS'), ~ as.numeric(.)) %>% 
  select(Species, ID, ITC, VOR, POS) %>% 
  rename(strain = ID, itc = ITC, pos = POS, vrc = VOR, species = Species) %>% 
  mutate(origin = 'Clinical', location = 'California', strain = as.character(strain)) %>% 
  mutate(across(c(species), ~ gsub('A.', 'aspergillus ', .x)))

# Combine all metadata
t <- full_join(info_df, calif_df) %>% 
  left_join(variant_info)

```

# Combine datasets

We combine the California clinical data with the primary metadata and link it to the genomic pairs.

```{r pressure, echo=T}

# Create a matching table for join operations
matching_df <- t %>% 
  select(strain, origin) %>% 
  rename(match = strain, origin_match = origin)

# Filter for high-similarity pairs (Clonal threshold: DST > 0.998)
df <- plink_df %>% 
  filter(DST > 0.998) %>% 
  rename(strain = FID1, match = FID2) %>% 
  left_join(t) %>% 
  select(strain, match, DST, origin, source, year_of_isolation, location) %>% 
  left_join(matching_df)

# Cleanup temporary objects
rm(variant_info, info_df, calif_df, matching_df)
```

# Network analysis (clustering)
Using the igraph package, we treat isolates as nodes and high-similarity pairs as edges to identify connected components (Clonal Groups).

```{r networking}
edges <- df[, c("strain", "match")]
g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE)
clusters <- components(g)

# Create the initial lookup
clonal_groups <- data.frame(
    strain = names(clusters$membership),
    group_id = as.vector(clusters$membership)
)

# Calculate sizes and create the RANK
group_ranks <- clonal_groups %>%
  group_by(group_id) %>%
  summarise(strains_count = n()) %>%
  # Sort by size descending, then assign new IDs 1, 2, 3...
  arrange(desc(strains_count)) %>%
  mutate(new_cg_id = paste0("CG", row_number()),
         order_id = row_number())

# Merge everything back together
df_final <- clonal_groups %>%
  left_join(group_ranks, by = "group_id") %>%
  left_join(t, by = "strain") %>% # Assuming 't' has the strain metadata
  select(
    order_id,
    group_id= new_cg_id, # Use our new ranked ID
    strains_count, 
    strain, 
    location, 
    origin, 
    variant, 
    itc, 
    pos, 
    vrc,
    teb,
    pro,
    dif,
    pth,
    year_of_isolation,
    specimen_types
  ) %>%
  mutate( group_id = fct_reorder(group_id, order_id)) %>%   arrange(order_id, strain) %>% select(-order_id)
# Export results
dir_path = here::here("results")
write.csv(df_final, glue::glue('{dir_path}/clonal_groups.csv'), row.names = T)

df_table4 <- df_final %>% 
  filter(group_id %in% c("CG1","CG2","CG3")) %>% 
  select(group_id,strain, origin, year_of_isolation,specimen_types,variant, itc:pth)
write.csv(df_table4, glue::glue('{dir_path}/table4_clonal_groups.csv'), row.names = T,dec = ',',sep = ';')
#library(openxlsx)
#write.xlsx(df_final, glue::glue('{dir_path}/clonal_groups.xlsx'),rowNames = T)


```

# Cluster exploration
We identify "Shared Clusters"—those containing isolates from different locations or different origins (Clinical vs. Environmental).
```{r clustering, echo =T}
# Clusters spanning California and other locations
cluster_info_location <- df_final %>% 
  group_by(group_id) %>%
  filter(any(location == "California") & any(location != "California"))

cat("\nClonal Groups with mixed locations (California vs Others):\n")
sort(unique(cluster_info_location$group_id))

```

```{r clustering2, echo =T}
# Clusters spanning Clinical and Environmental origins
cluster_info_origin <- df_final %>% 
  group_by(group_id) %>%
  filter(any(origin == "Clinical") & any(origin == "Environmental"))

# View IDs of interesting clusters
cat("Clonal Groups with mixed origins:\n")
sort(unique(cluster_info_origin$group_id))

```

# Cluster plots
Finally, an overview of three plots is made with various x-axes to view cluster data

```{r plotting, echo = F, warning=F}

filling ='#01689b'
cols = '#01689b'
alp = 0.8
p1 =ggplot(plink_df) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x=DST),bins=400,fill=filling, color = cols,alpha = alp) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x="Genetic Distance",y="Pairs")

#now make plots
p2 =ggplot(plink_df) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x=DST),bins=400,,fill=filling, color = cols ,alpha = alp) + xlim(0.88,1) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x="Genetic Distance",y="Pairs")

p3 = ggplot(plink_df) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x=DST),bins=400,,fill=filling, color =cols ,alpha = alp) + xlim(0.995,1) +
  theme_classic() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=0.998),lty=2)+
  labs(x="Genetic Distance",y="Pairs")

plots <- (p1 + p2 + p3 ) + plot_layout(ncol = 1)
plots
```

Saving plots:
```{r save plots}
dir_path = here::here("plots")
ggsave(filename =glue::glue("{dir_path}/S4_genetic_distances.svg"), plot = plots,  width = 8,  height = 6,   bg = "white")

```
